chunk_findings.detail: This doc instructs running the live ACP probe by passing an arbitrary external agent command string (`'kilo acp'`) to `probes/probe_acp_mcp_inject.py`; that path executes the external `acp` dependency directly instead of through a `ddflow/adapters` port. This violates [r-adapters], which says anything outside our own process or the stdlib, including `acp` and subprocess tools, must go through one adapter port so tests and kits can substitute a fake and swaps touch one place.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/control-planes.md:30

chunk_findings.detail: The new sentence points readers to `templates/control_plane_facts.toml`, but the actual file added by this change is `ddflow/templates/control_plane_facts.toml` (as listed in the manifest). Since the same paragraph uses a repo-root-relative path for `docs/ddflow/research/control-planes.md`, `templates/control_plane_facts.toml` resolves to `docs/ddflow/templates/control_plane_facts.toml`, which does not exist. A user following the documentation will look in the wrong place and not find the shipped control-plane facts template.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adding-a-harness.md:30

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `if not harness:` means `PF.rows(planes, agent)` is skipped whenever `agent` resolves to an existing Harness. The preceding validation explicitly allows an id that is absent from `HR` but present in `PF.ids(planes)`, so the two namespaces are accepted as alternatives—but an id present in both is silently truncated. For example, if `paseo` is both a registered harness and a control-plane fact in `control_plane_facts.toml`, calling `harness_facts("paseo")` returns only the harness rows and omits the matching control-plane facts, contradicting the function’s own contract that the table contains “every descriptor value and control-plane fact.” The plane rows should be added based on `agent in PF.ids(planes)`, not on the truthiness of `harness`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness.py:harness_facts

chunk_findings.detail: A local `.ddflow/control_plane_facts.toml` that is valid TOML but not a top-level table, such as `[]`, makes `_merge` call `extra.get(...)` on a list, raising `AttributeError`. `load` catches only `TomlError` and `OSError`, so the user gets a raw traceback instead of the documented `FactsError` for a bad local facts file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/planefacts.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: `problems` assumes every item under `plane` is itself a dict and calls `sorted(row.items())`. A parsed facts file with a non-table plane entry, e.g. `problems({"plane": {"broken": []}})`, raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items'` instead of returning a defect string. Its own docstring says it returns every defect of a parsed facts file, so the validator is not safe for malformed inputs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/planefacts.py:problems

chunk_findings.detail: This file accesses the filesystem layout directly with `pathlib.Path` / `Path.is_file` rather than through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, which [r-adapters] requires for filesystem access so it can be swapped or faked. The direct use makes this new service avoid the project’s adapter boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/planefacts.py:39-40 [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: The file's own header comment states: `none` = looked for and absent at that commit, no `v`. However, the fact `mcp_inject` under `[plane.harness-remote]` has `s = "none"` but also provides a `v` field describing what the code sends (`mcpServers: []`). This contradicts the declared record contract, and any consumer or validation logic that treats a `none` fact as having no value field will break or produce incorrect output on this entry.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/control_plane_facts.toml: [plane.harness-remote] mcp_inject

chunk_findings.detail: When `agent` names an existing harness, `harness` is truthy, so the condition `if not harness:` is false and `PF.rows(planes, agent)` is never called. For example, with a harness named `paseo` registered in `HR`, `harness facts paseo` returns only `HF.rows` for that harness and drops all control-plane facts for it. That contradicts the function’s own contract: “every descriptor value and control-plane fact.” The control-plane facts are only added when the selected id is a plane or when no agent is given, so a user asking for a specific harness gets incomplete facts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness.py:harness_facts

chunk_findings.detail: `_merge` merges a project override row into the base fact with `planes.setdefault(name, {}).update(row)`, which only overwrites keys present in the override and leaves absent keys from the shipped fact. A project cannot turn an existing fact with a `v` into a `s = "none"` tombstone: the override row omits `v`, but the old `v` remains from the base fact. `load` then calls `problems`, which reports `status none takes no value`, and raises `FactsError`. This makes the required remove-as-tombstone record behavior impossible for value-bearing shipped facts. [r-everything-managed]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/planefacts.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: `problems` assumes every value under `data["plane"]` is a dict and calls `row.items()`. A parsed TOML document like `[plane]\nbad = "oops"` gives `data = {"plane": {"bad": "oops"}}`; line 79 then raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'` instead of returning a defect string, contradicting the function’s contract that every defect of a parsed facts file is reported as one string.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/planefacts.py:79

chunk_findings.detail: The file declares “The facts themselves live in one place, `ddflow/templates/control_plane_facts.toml`” and “`ddflow harness facts` renders them in the one facts table.” That creates a separate generated facts table and renderer outside `HX-facts-core`, but the task note `RH-contradictions-2026-10-18` (contradiction #25) says `HX-facts-core` owns the generated facts record and table with confidence; this task must either fill that table or keep only its own control-plane probes. By documenting this separate facts store as the single place, the change points downstream work at the wrong system and contradicts the stated ownership boundary.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/control-planes.md:5-8

chunk_findings.detail: If the probe is launched with `CP_PROBE_MARKER=injected` in its own environment, `env = {**os.environ, "HOME": str(home)}` keeps that variable. The stub logs `marker=injected`, so an ACP agent that ignores the injected `mcpServers[0].env` entry but inherits its current environment when spawning the server will still make `judge.env_passed` true. The probe then exits 0 and records a false verified fact. The marker should be removed from `env` before spawning the agent, or an unpredictable per-run value should be used.
chunk_findings.title: probes/probe_acp_mcp_inject.py: env construction

chunk_findings.detail: The new probe directly reaches outside the process for subprocess spawning, filesystem layout, environment, and clocks instead of using the `ddflow/adapters` ports required by [r-adapters]. This bypasses the one-port-per-external-dependency decision and prevents tests from substituting a fake adapter for the agent and temp-dir behavior.
chunk_findings.title: probes/probe_acp_mcp_inject.py: subprocess/os/tempfile/time use

chunk_findings.detail: `problems` is documented to return every defect of a parsed facts file as strings, but a successful TOML parse of a bad file is not always a table-of-tables. Given `{"plane": {"acp": "nope"}}` or `{"plane": "x"}` (what `plane = "x"` / a non-table `acp` value parses to), `sorted(data.get("plane", {}).items())` or `row.items()` raises TypeError before any defect string is produced. `_merge` rejects that shape only on the project-override path, so a direct `problems(io.read(...))` — the validator the tests call — cannot name the defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/planefacts.py:problems

chunk_findings.detail: `FactsError` is specified to name the project file that cannot be used, and `load` does that for `TomlError`/`OSError` and for `problems()` hits (`f"{local}: ..."`). Structural failures raised inside `_merge` do not. Given `/proj/.ddflow/control_plane_facts.toml` containing `plane = "x"`, `load(Path("/proj"))` raises `FactsError("control_plane_facts.toml: [plane] is not a table")` with only the basename, which is also the shipped template's name, so the failure is attributed to the wrong file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/planefacts.py:_merge

chunk_findings.detail: `plane.acp-codex.adapter` sets `src = "codex-acp-old"` (zed-industries/codex-acp@296069e84163, marked archived) while `v` is `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` at `ver = "2.5.0"`. The same table’s `inject_mcp`/`cwd` rows cite `codex-acp-src` for that package and version, and the note says the archived repo only redirects there. A lookup that follows `src` therefore reads the wrong tree for a `documented` fact (the file’s own rule: documented means read at the pinned `[sources]` commit).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/control_plane_facts.toml:72

chunk_findings.detail: `plane.harness-remote.upstream` claims `github.com/giuliastro/harness-remote` at `ver = "3.8.0"` with `s = "documented"` but `src = "hr-fork"` (monperrus/harness-remote, stale fork). Sibling rows that actually describe 3.8.0 cite `hr-src`. Documented status is defined as read from that source’s pinned commit, not from a GitHub fork relationship, so replaying the cited source does not establish the stated upstream or version.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/control_plane_facts.toml:45

chunk_findings.detail: The MCP stub is not a spec stdio server, and success does not require a handshake. MCP stdio (the `2024-11-05` version the stub itself echoes) frames messages as `Content-Length` headers, not bare JSON lines. On the first client line `Content-Length: …`, `json.loads` raises, the stub dies, and replies at line 48 are unframed so a compliant agent cannot read them. `probe` still returns 0 whenever the process merely started with the marker and `cwd == session` (line 141), because `initialized` / `tools_listed` are ignored. A real agent that honours injection and speaks MCP therefore either crashes the stub or fails the handshake, yet the probe can still exit 0 and mark the fact verified; a blank line or any non-JSON frame does the same after the `started` log line is written.
chunk_findings.title: probes/probe_acp_mcp_inject.py:32
